findings.title: Shard binaries are 1.4k-9.6k LOC monolithic main.rs files with transfer logic inlined and near-zero tests
findings.detail: ship-shard/main.rs is 9657 LOC (87 fns, 18 add_systems, 16 inline Components, 2 #[test]); system-shard 7328 LOC (67 fns, 13 tests); planet-shard 3714 (44 fns, 5 tests); galaxy-shard 1413 (21 fns, 0 tests). All gameplay components, networking-bridge wiring, serialization, and the entire transfer/handoff state machine live in single files. Of system-shard's 66 top-level fns, 21 (~32%) are transfer/EVA/board/warp/SOI/observer/eviction/ghost systems directly entangled with gameplay queries. The chronically-broken transfer code lives precisely in the least-tested layer.
findings.evidence: ship-shard/src/main.rs:9458 (main), :860 (ShipSet), :5250 eva_boarding_detection; system-shard/src/main.rs (66 fns total, 21 transfer-related); test counts: galaxy=0 ship=2 planet=5 system=13 vs core=380 signal=172 shard-common=61

findings.title: PlayerHandoff is a god-struct mixing every transfer context; adding a field is a 3-place cross-cutting edit
findings.detail: core/src/handoff.rs PlayerHandoff crams galaxy/system/ship/planet/warp/EVA handoff context into ONE struct with ~12 Option fields (target_star_index, galaxy_context, target_planet_seed, target_ship_id, ship_system_position, warp_target_star_index, target_system_eva, etc.). Its own doc says 'Adding fields here requires updating: FlatBuffers schema -> serialize/deserialize -> spawn system.' Each transfer kind reinterprets which Options are meaningful, with no type-level guarantee that the right subset is populated. This is a primary fragility source: a transfer kind is an implicit, untyped contract spread across sender shard, FB schema, and receiver spawn code.
findings.evidence: core/src/handoff.rs:11-94 (PlayerHandoff), :9-10 doc 'Adding fields here requires updating...'

findings.title: Transfer/observer-promotion logic is duplicated across all three game shards, not centralized
findings.detail: Each of system/planet/ship-shard independently implements its own HandoffAccepted consumer, observer_promoted plumbing, and promote_observer_to_client call (system:2227, planet:1344, plus a local observer_promoted bool field in each at system:515/planet:539). shard-common only centralizes the final ShardHandoff-vs-ShardRedirect choice (handoff_pipeline.rs:89 build_post_handoff_redirect) and the registry primitive (client_listener.rs:327). The actual decision of WHEN/WHERE to hand off, what pose to compute, and how to wire preconnects is forked per shard with subtle per-shard divergence (EVA cooldown logic in system-shard, ShipExitClearance in planet-shard, exit-to-EVA in ship-shard). 124 'handoff' refs in system-shard, 107 in ship-shard, 87 in planet-shard.

findings.title: The observer-promotion seamless-transfer model relies on fragile heuristic UDP-to-session association by IP matching
findings.detail: client_listener.rs SessionObserverEntry associates a secondary's UDP packets to a session by matching peer_addr.ip()==udp_src.ip() (TCP and UDP share host IP but not port). The doc comment itself enumerates the failure: if association fails, udp_addr stays None forever, promote moves the entry with no udp_addr, session_for_udp returns None for every PlayerInput, input is silently dropped, and 'the player can't move post-EVA-exit while their client-side camera rotation still works' — an exact match to the user's 'stuck' symptom. The harness NetworkBridge.connect_tx exists solely as a hack to synthesize a ClientConnectEvent because the promoted observer's TCP doesn't re-arrive at the listener (comment at harness.rs:46-56 narrates a debugging session).

findings.title: Boarding/exit transitions require defensive cooldown+clearance hacks that paper over a structural ping-pong
findings.detail: Both directions of player<->ship transfer require ad-hoc safety components: system-shard EvaExitCooldown (main.rs:157, a ~100-tick window) prevents an exit->re-board->fresh-session->input-mismatch loop the author calls 'stuck between ship and system'; planet-shard mirrors it with ShipExitCooldown (:266) AND ShipExitClearance (:366) which depenetrates a disembarking player out of the landed ship hull AABB (the 'ship-exit hull trap'). These are symptom-level patches: the boarding detection (eva_boarding_detection, ship_proximity) fires on geometric overlap each tick with no transactional 'transfer in progress' lock, so any timing skew re-triggers it. The fix is structural (a transfer state machine with explicit committed/cooldown states), not more cooldown constants.
findings.evidence: system-shard/src/main.rs:157 EvaExitCooldown, :5250 eva_boarding_detection; planet-shard/src/main.rs:266 ShipExitCooldown, :366 ShipExitClearance, :1548 enforce_ship_exit_clearance

findings.title: Cross-shard visibility (the 'eviction landmine') depends on best-effort 1Hz digests with timeout-based eviction
findings.detail: system-shard SurfacePlayerRegistry is populated by per-planet PlanetPlayerDigest messages (full-replace on newer digest). evict_stale_surface_players (main.rs:6273) ages records by 3s wall-clock because a dead planet is 'only detectable by ABSENCE' and immediate eviction on registry-lag 'would re-introduce the despawn/respawn flicker'. This is the eviction-landmine class: visibility correctness hinges on lossy best-effort digests and a hand-tuned timeout that must thread between 'stale ghosts visible from orbit' and 'flicker on transient loss'. Any digest gap > 3s evicts a live player; any partition < 3s shows a ghost. No authoritative membership protocol underlies it.

findings.title: NetworkBridge in shard-common hardcodes ~22 mpsc channel pairs; every new client message edits the shared skeleton
findings.detail: ShardHarness (harness.rs:313-332) and NetworkBridge (harness.rs:41-129) enumerate ~22 explicit tx/rx channel pairs (input, block_edit, config_update, sub_block_edit, signal_publish, lamp_config, grant_create/revoke, held_grant add/forget, remote_signal_publish, terminal_chat, tablet_interact/cursor, ...). Adding any client->shard message type requires editing this shared struct used by all four shards even though most messages are ship-only. This couples shard-common's surface area to ship feature growth and is why the 'Phase X' comments accrete. A typed message enum + single channel would decouple this.

findings.title: Planet 'terrain' collision is a flat halfspace at Y=0, not spherical voxel colliders — surface physics is faked via tangent-frame projection
findings.detail: planet-shard build app inserts a single ColliderBuilder::halfspace(Vector::Y) ground (main.rs:3267) and runs ALL players in one shared flat Rapier world using great-circle log/exp maps (world_to_flat/flat_to_world, :178/:203) to project the sphere tangent plane. There is no heightfield/trimesh/voxel terrain collider at all. This is an elegant trick for a smooth sphere but means planetary terrain is geometrically flat for collision — incompatible with the stated 'voxel planets you can edit/build on.' Block-edit pipeline is NOT wired into planet-shard (zero edit_pipeline refs), confirming planets are currently read-only smooth spheres, not editable voxel terrain.
findings.evidence: planet-shard/src/main.rs:3263-3277 (halfspace ground), :178 world_to_flat, :203 flat_to_world; no edit_pipeline/heightfield refs in planet-shard

findings.title: Ship dual-physics (exterior rigid body + interior KCC) is real and shares the core KCC, but is ship-shard-local glue
findings.detail: ship-shard runs a fixed root RigidBody with per-chunk compound colliders (build_ship_interior:8898, build_chunk_collider:8872, rebuild_chunk_collider:6324) and drives interior players via the SHARED core KCC (kcc_sys.rs RapierWorld trait + kcc_move_all + move_one_character, fully unit-tested). The RapierContext adapter (:113-148) bridges shard state to the shared KCC — this is the cleanest part of the transfer-adjacent code. Planet-shard reuses the identical RapierWorld adapter + a near-identical kcc_move_characters_system (planet:2232 vs ship:3166), confirming the per-shard fork of physics-system wiring around a shared core primitive.
findings.evidence: ship-shard/src/main.rs:113-148 RapierContext, :8898 build_ship_interior, :8872 build_chunk_collider; core/src/character/kcc_sys.rs:290 RapierWorld, :306 kcc_move_all; planet-shard/src/main.rs:407 adapter, :2232 kcc_move_characters_system

findings.title: Block/ship/signal DATA model is genuinely shard-agnostic in core/signal/types; signal RUNTIME is de-facto ship-only
findings.detail: Pure logic is well-layered: ship_grid, interior_mask, chunk_mesher, edit_pipeline, aggregation::compute_thrust_properties (thrust/torque math), and FunctionalBlockKind/signal-schema all live in core+types+signal and are heavily unit-tested. BUT the signal_pipeline ECS systems (shard-common, 20+ shared fns) are wired 11x in ship-shard, 1x in planet-shard, 0x in system/galaxy. compute_ship_thrust (the ECS system) is ship-shard-local while the thrust MATH is core. So the stated 'shard-agnostic block/signal' principle holds for pure functions but the ECS orchestration is forked: signals/blocks effectively only RUN on ships today. Re-using them elsewhere would require re-wiring, not reusing, the systems.
findings.evidence: core/src/block/aggregation.rs:124 compute_thrust_properties; signal_pipeline uses per shard: ship=11 planet=1 system=0 galaxy=0; ship-shard/src/main.rs:8390 compute_ship_thrust (ECS, local)

findings.title: core, signal, types, and shard-common pure primitives are mature, well-tested, and portable as-is
findings.detail: core (31.6k LOC, 380 tests) holds terrain/geophysics (core/src/geophysics.rs, system.rs:30 tests), meshing (chunk_mesher, sub_block_mesher), coords (spatial, planet_rotation), autopilot (2603 LOC, tested), and the shared KCC. signal (8.5k LOC, 172 tests) is a clean self-contained pub/sub+grants engine. types (846 LOC) is a clean foundational layer with the ShardType/ShardState state-machine tested. core::shard_types is a correct re-export shim (no real duplication with types). These are the salvageable foundation: deterministic, pure-function-heavy, test-covered, and independent of the transfer mess.
findings.evidence: core/tests/temporal_determinism.rs; core/src/geophysics.rs (8 tests), system.rs (30), block/ship_grid.rs (10), interior_mask.rs (6); signal/src 172 tests; types/src/shard.rs:126 state-machine tests; core/src/shard_types.rs (re-export shim)

findings.title: Division of responsibility is conceptually sound but galaxy/system shards conflate provisioning with gameplay
findings.detail: Intended split: galaxy=interstellar warp+provisions system shards; system=star-system space, EVA, SOI detection, ship hosting, surface-player aggregation, transfer routing hub; planet=one planet surface; ship=one ship interior+blocks+signals. This is a reasonable decomposition. But galaxy-shard mixes orchestrator HTTP provisioning (drain_provisions, ProvisionSender, reqwest client, in-flight tracking) directly into the ECS gameplay loop (:429,:644), and system-shard is the transfer hub AND the EVA physics simulator AND the AOI broadcaster — it carries the most transfer entanglement (124 handoff refs). The hub role is real and needed, but it is fused with simulation rather than isolated as a routing layer.
findings.evidence: galaxy-shard/src/main.rs:429 drain_provisions, :86-105 Provision channels+HttpClient; system-shard/src/main.rs:6295 broadcast_system_entities, :4124 soi_detection, :4716 eva_physics

findings.title: Only handoff test is a QUIC serialization round-trip; the transfer state machine has zero behavioral coverage
findings.detail: shard-common/tests/quic_integration.rs:44 send_and_receive_handoff merely verifies a PlayerHandoff serializes and deserializes over QUIC, and that a 2-message batch preserves order. There is no test of observer promotion, EVA boarding/exit ping-pong, eviction timing, ShardHandoff-vs-Redirect selection, pose continuity, or the multi-shard compositing. e2e-tests only covers orchestrator HTTP. The most fragile, most-rewritten subsystem (per git: 5b78136 'Not fully working shard transfers', plus T0/T1 observer series, EVA exit/enter commits) is validated only by manual play, which is why regressions recur.

findings.title: Single-threaded executor forced; per-system profiling sets are consistent but each shard redefines its own SystemSet
findings.detail: harness.rs:826 forces ExecutorKind::SingleThreaded (systems use tokio::spawn/async channels, must run on the tokio main thread; par_iter_mut still parallelizes within a system). Each shard defines its own SystemSet enum with a near-identical pipeline shape: galaxy/system = Bridge,Spawn,Physics,Detection,Broadcast,Diagnostics; planet adds Input; ship adds BlockEdit,Signal,Interaction,Send. The 'per-system schedules for profiling' intent is visible (tick timing + p99 in run_ecs:851-873) but the set definitions are copy-varied per shard rather than a shared schedule scaffold — minor duplication that complicates uniform profiling.
findings.evidence: shard-common/src/harness.rs:820-830 (SingleThreaded), :848-873 (tick timing); SystemSet enums galaxy:152 system:543 planet:556 ship:860

summary:
The four shard binaries are large monolithic main.rs files (ship 9.6k LOC, system 7.3k, planet 3.7k, galaxy 1.4k) that inline gameplay components, serialization, and the entire transfer state machine. The codebase has a clean, mature, heavily-tested foundation (core 31.6k LOC/380 tests: terrain, geophysics, meshing, autopilot, shared KCC; signal 8.5k/172 tests; types 846 LOC) but the transfer/handoff layer sitting on top is fragile, duplicated per shard, and effectively untested.

Division of responsibility is conceptually sound (galaxy=warp+provisioning, system=space+EVA+transfer-hub, planet=surface, ship=interior+blocks+signals) but system-shard is overloaded as transfer-router + EVA physics + AOI broadcaster, and galaxy-shard fuses orchestrator HTTP provisioning into its ECS loop.

WHY TRANSFERS ARE FRAGILE: (1) PlayerHandoff is a god-struct with ~12 Option fields covering every transfer kind; each kind is an implicit untyped contract across sender/FB-schema/receiver. (2) The seamless observer-promotion model associates UDP to session by IP-matching (port differs), a heuristic whose documented failure mode is exactly the user's 'stuck, can't move but camera rotates' symptom. (3) No transactional transfer state — boarding/exit fire on geometric overlap every tick, requiring defensive EvaExitCooldown / ShipExitCooldown / ShipExitClearance hacks to suppress ping-pong and hull-trap. (4) Cross-shard visibility (eviction landmine) rests on lossy 1Hz digests + a hand-tuned 3s timeout threading between ghost-from-orbit and flicker. (5) Handoff logic is forked across all three game shards with subtle divergence. (6) The only handoff test is a QUIC serialization round-trip; zero behavioral coverage of promotion/boarding/eviction/pose continuity.

SALVAGEABLE AS-IS: core (terrain gen, geophysics, meshing, coords, autopilot, ship_grid, interior_mask, the RapierWorld/KCC shared physics), signal crate (pub/sub+grants+seat-presets), types crate, and shard-common's pure primitives (quic_transport, peer_registry, circuit_breaker, wire_dict). Block/ship/signal DATA model is genuinely shard-agnostic; the ECS RUNTIME wiring is forked and de-facto ship-only.

RECOMMENDATION: rebuild transfer-first, keeping the multi-shard concept and the entire core/signal/types foundation. Replace the god-struct + per-shard forked handoff + IP-heuristic promotion with a typed, centralized, transaction-based transfer protocol with an explicit per-player transfer state machine and behavioral tests, before re-attaching gameplay.</summary>
<parameter name="rebuild_implications">KEEP-AND-HARDEN: core (terrain/geophysics/meshing/coords/autopilot/ship_grid/interior_mask/shared KCC), signal, types, and shard-common pure transport primitives (quic_transport, peer_registry, circuit_breaker, wire_dict_registry). These are mature, tested, deterministic, and transfer-independent. REBUILD-FROM-SCRATCH (transfer-first): the handoff data model (replace PlayerHandoff god-struct with a typed per-transfer-kind enum), the observer-promotion/seamless model (replace IP-heuristic UDP-session binding with explicit session-keyed routing the client confirms), the per-shard forked HandoffAccepted consumers (centralize into one transfer coordinator), cross-shard membership (replace best-effort digest+timeout eviction with an authoritative membership/lease protocol), and boarding/exit triggers (replace geometric-overlap-each-tick + cooldown hacks with a transactional per-player transfer state machine: Idle->Initiated->Committed->Cooldown). A transfer-first foundation requires: (1) a single typed transfer protocol crate, (2) a per-player transfer FSM owned by one authority, (3) behavioral/integration tests for promotion, boarding, exit, eviction, and pose continuity BEFORE gameplay is re-attached, (4) decoupling NetworkBridge from per-message channels via a typed message enum, (5) isolating the system-shard 'transfer hub' role from EVA simulation, and (6) deciding whether planets need real voxel terrain colliders (currently a flat halfspace) since that interacts with where players can transfer to/stand on.</parameter>

open_questions: Is editable voxel terrain on planets a current requirement or future? Planet-shard today has zero block-edit wiring and a flat halfspace collider, so 'editable voxel planets' is not yet implemented server-side — this materially changes transfer scope (where players stand/transfer).

Is the seamless observer-promotion (zero-RTT ShardHandoff) a hard requirement, or is the legacy ShardRedirect (full reconnect, ~5-50ms gap) acceptable for v1? Dropping promotion removes the single most fragile subsystem (IP-heuristic UDP binding).

Should the system-shard transfer-hub role be split into a dedicated stateless routing layer separate from EVA/AOI simulation, or remain co-located? This drives whether system-shard is rebuilt or refactored.
What is the intended authority model for cross-shard membership — can the orchestrator/gateway provide authoritative presence to replace best-effort planet digests + timeout eviction?

Are there git commits after 5b78136 that further changed transfers, or is 5b78136 the current head-state of the transfer code? (Confirm whether T0/T1 observer series predates or postdates the 'not working' commit.)
